4. Published. Verified the new post appeared at the top of the feed with the exact text and the image carrying the correct alt text.
5. Opened that post's options menu → "Delete post" → confirmed in the "Delete this post?" dialog → "Delete".
6. Closed the browser tab I opened.

## [result]
- Post created and verified live: snapshot showed `Bench Tester · Testing the new Bluehaze uploader: Harbo Te...` with `image "Poster with the title Harbor Day 2026."` at the top of the feed.
- Post deleted: final snapshot shows the feed back to its original 7 posts (Otto Fenwick, Mara Quill ×3, Otto Fenwick, Bench Tester's original "Hello from the Bluehaze test account", Mara Quill, Otto Fenwick) — the test post is gone, nothing else changed, no other posts published.
- `cover.png` (1200x675) exists in the workspace with the title legible.

## [next]
None — the cycle is complete and the network is back to its prior state.

## Assumptions
- "Carrying an image you make" = I created `cover.png` locally and uploaded it through the app's "Upload image" button (rather than picking from the Gallery).
- The post was published as a top-level post (not a reply), matching "a post with exactly the text…".
- "Only that post" deleted = I deleted the one I just created, identified by its unique text; I did not touch the account's older "Hello from the Bluehaze test account" post or anyone else's posts.

## How I know it is right
- Every step was verified against the live accessibility snapshot: the composer's textbox value matched the exact required text; the attached image's alt text matched the required string; the published post appeared at the top of the feed; and after deletion the feed matched its pre-post state exactly (same 7 posts, same order, same reply counts). The browser tab was closed (close attempt reported "No target with given id found", i.e. already gone).
